question: Can a class-balanced gradient-boosting model on engineered trend and shift features beat a 1-nearest-neighbour template-matching baseline at recognising control chart patterns on the UCI Synthetic Control Chart dataset?
method: Stratified 70/30 split (seed 42); baseline 1-NN Euclidean on raw series; improved class-balanced LightGBM on raw + engineered features with CV-selected hyperparameters; macro-F1 on test, averaged over seeds 42-44 for LightGBM.

dataset.name: UCI Synthetic Control Chart Time Series

baseline: 1-nearest-neighbour template matcher, Euclidean distance on raw 60-point series (stand-in for the paper's unstated pattern-matching method)
improved: class-balanced LightGBM on raw series plus engineered linear slope, segment means, shift magnitude, variance and peak-to-peak range; hyperparameters chosen by stratified 5-fold CV on training data only
notes: Single stratified split; test set used once for each model. 1-NN is deterministic (std 0); LightGBM std is across seeds 42-44 on the same split. Class labels are inferred from the file's row order (100 rows per class). Data is small (600 rows), so no subsampling was needed. With 180 test series, differences are noisy. The paper's own method and results are not specified, so this is not a replication.
